title: 7 Warnings You Should Never Ignore About Finances in Church
paragraphs: 7 Warnings You Should Never Ignore About Finances in Church
There are people sitting in church every Sunday carrying financial wounds nobody can see.
Some smile while drowning in debt.
Some give publicly but secretly resent God privately.
Some pastors preach faith while silently suffocating under pressure to maintain appearances.
Some ministries look successful online but are spiritually collapsing behind closed doors because money slowly replaced obedience.
And some believers were never taught the difference between biblical stewardship and spiritual manipulation.
This conversation is uncomfortable.
But it is necessary.
Because money has destroyed churches.
Money has divided families.
Money has corrupted leaders.
Money has turned altars into stages.
And if we are honest… some people no longer know whether they are following Jesus Christ or following religious systems built on financial performance.
The Bible never avoids this subject.
Jesus Himself spoke about money constantly because finances reveal what the heart worships.
In Matthew 6:21, Jesus says:
“For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”
The Greek word for “treasure” is θησαυρός (thēsauros).
It means a storehouse.
A treasury.
A place where someone deposits what they value most.
Jesus was not merely discussing coins.
He was exposing worship.
Because whatever controls your treasure eventually controls your heart.
And that is why the enemy attacks finances so aggressively inside churches.
Not because money itself is evil.
But because love of money becomes an idol powerful enough to compete with surrender to God.
The Apostle Paul warned Timothy with terrifying clarity.
1 Timothy 6:10 says:
“For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil.”
The Greek phrase for “love of money” is φιλαργυρία (philargyria).
It literally means affection for silver.
An unhealthy devotion to wealth.
Notice Paul did not say money is evil.
He said the obsession with it opens doors to destruction.
And history proves him right.
Churches have split over money.
Friendships have died over offerings.
Pastors have fallen because of greed.
Families have abandoned faith because manipulation disguised itself as ministry.
So before another generation confuses biblical stewardship with spiritual exploitation…
These warnings must be spoken clearly.
And some of them may hit closer to home than expected.
Someone else may be silently fighting the exact same battle.
The first warning is using giving to manipulate God.
Some people were taught that every financial seed guarantees earthly wealth.
That if they give enough, God becomes obligated to bless them materially.
But that is not biblical covenant.
That is transactional religion.
In Acts 8, Simon the Sorcerer tried to purchase spiritual power.
Peter rebuked him fiercely:
“May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money.”
The Greek word used for perish is ἀπώλεια (apōleia).
It means destruction.
Ruin.
Loss.
Peter understood something dangerous.
The moment people think money can control God, repentance disappears.
Giving is worship.
Not bribery.
You cannot purchase the Holy Spirit.
You cannot buy anointing.
You cannot manipulate heaven with offerings.
God is not a vending machine responding to financial pressure.
And yes… God blesses generosity.
But biblical blessing is deeper than cars, houses, or public success.
Sometimes blessing looks like peace during suffering.
Sometimes blessing looks like freedom from greed.
Sometimes blessing looks like surviving a season that should have destroyed you.
And sometimes the greatest blessing is God refusing to give you what would have become your idol.
The second warning is pressuring the poor while protecting the wealthy.
James directly confronted favoritism inside the church.
James 2:2-4 exposes believers who honored rich people while humiliating the poor.
The Greek word προσωπολημψία (prosōpolēmpsia) means partiality.
Favoritism based on external status.
Some churches still do this today.
A wealthy donor receives influence.
A struggling single mother becomes invisible.
A businessman gets platform access.
A broken believer gets ignored.
But heaven does not measure people by net worth.
Jesus Himself was born among the poor.
The King of Glory entered earth in humility.
Not luxury.
Church becomes spiritually dangerous when money determines honor.
Because eventually leaders stop hearing God and start protecting financial power.
And that corruption spreads quietly.
The third warning is living beyond your means to appear “blessed.”
This one hurts because social media intensified it.
Many believers are financially exhausted trying to maintain appearances.
Expensive lifestyles.
Designer image.
Forced success.
Fake prosperity.
Meanwhile anxiety grows privately.
Proverbs 22:7 says:
“The borrower is servant to the lender.”
The Hebrew word for servant is עֶבֶד (‘eved).
Bondman.
Slave.
Debt itself is not automatically sin.
But bondage becomes dangerous when image matters more than wisdom.
Some believers buy things to impress people they secretly envy.
Others overspend because they are emotionally empty.
And some ministry leaders feel trapped trying to sustain an image of constant success.
But pretending to be blessed while secretly drowning destroys peace.
God never called believers to fake prosperity.
He called them to faithful stewardship.
There is no shame in simplicity.
There is no shame in rebuilding.
There is no shame in saying:
“I need financial wisdom.”
The fourth warning is exploiting generosity for personal gain.
This is one of the most devastating wounds in modern Christianity.
Because spiritual authority carries sacred responsibility.
Ezekiel 34 rebukes shepherds who fed themselves instead of the flock.
And sadly, history keeps repeating.
Some leaders use fear to control giving.
Some manipulate vulnerable people emotionally.
Some build personal kingdoms while calling it ministry.
And some believers gave sacrificially only to later discover corruption behind the scenes.
That pain is real.
But abuse does not erase biblical generosity.
It reveals why accountability matters.
True shepherds protect people.
They do not consume them.
Paul told the Corinthians:
“For I seek not what is yours but you.”
A real spiritual leader values souls more than offerings.
Always.
The fifth warning is neglecting generosity entirely.
Some believers swing to the opposite extreme.
After seeing manipulation, they harden their hearts completely.
But Scripture still commands generosity.
Not because God needs money.
Because generosity transforms the human heart.
In 2 Corinthians 9:7:
“God loves a cheerful giver.”
The Greek word for cheerful is ἱλαρός (hilaros).
It means joyful.
Willing.
Glad-hearted.
Not pressured.
Not threatened.
Not guilted.
Biblical generosity flows from love.
And sometimes generosity is not even financial.
Sometimes it is feeding someone.
Helping quietly.
Supporting missions.
Paying for groceries.
Covering a struggling family in prayer and action.
The early church became powerful because believers cared for each other sacrificially.
And in a world obsessed with self-preservation… generosity still preaches the Gospel.
The sixth warning is trusting money more than God.
This can happen to rich people.
Poor people.
Church leaders.
Business owners.
Anyone.
Because money creates an illusion of security.
But economies collapse.
Jobs disappear.
Health changes.
Unexpected tragedy comes without warning.
Psalm 20:7 says:
“Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.”
Modern chariots simply changed forms.
Bank accounts.
Investments.
Status.
Connections.
Success.
None of those things are eternal.
Only Christ is.
And sometimes God allows uncomfortable seasons to expose where trust truly lives.
Because many people discover their faith was stable only while life felt financially secure.
The seventh warning is forgetting eternity completely.
This may be the most dangerous one.
Because entire lives can be consumed chasing temporary success.
Jesus asked:
“For what will it profit a man if he gains the whole world and forfeits his soul?”
The Greek word ψυχή (psychē) means soul.
Life.
Inner being.
A person can become financially successful and spiritually empty simultaneously.
And tragically… many do.
There are wealthy people who cannot sleep peacefully.
Successful people addicted secretly.
Influential people spiritually hollow.
Because nothing in creation can replace communion with God.
Not money.
Not applause.
Not influence.
Not possessions.
Only Jesus Christ satisfies the soul.
And deep down… many people reading this already know that.
Because no purchase healed the loneliness.
No paycheck removed the emptiness.
No material success silenced the fear.
Only the presence of God touches places money never can.
Maybe that is why this article found you.
Not to condemn you.
But to wake something up again.
To remind you that biblical stewardship is not merely about dollars.
It is about worship.
Trust.
Integrity.
Compassion.
Humility.
And surrender.
If you have been financially broken, manipulated, greedy, fearful, prideful, or exhausted… Jesus Christ still invites you closer.
Grace still exists.
Repentance still changes people.
Restoration still happens.
And your story is not over.
Be honest.
Someone else scrolling tonight may realize they are not alone because you chose vulnerability instead of silence.
One day, every dollar you touched will mean nothing… but every soul you helped lead toward Jesus Christ will echo into eternity.
Filipino Version:
7 Babala sa Pananalapi sa Simbahan na Hindi Mo Dapat Balewalain
May mga taong nakaupo sa loob ng simbahan tuwing Linggo na may dalang sugat sa pananalapi na walang nakakakita.
Ngumingiti sila… pero gabi-gabi umiiyak dahil sa utang.
Nagbibigay sila sa harap ng tao… pero palihim na nagtatanong sa Diyos kung bakit parang hindi naubos ang bigat.
May mga pastor na nangangaral tungkol sa pananampalataya habang lihim na dinudurog ng pressure na panatilihin ang imahe ng “pinagpapala.”
May mga ministry na mukhang matagumpay online pero sa likod ng kamera… unti-unti nang namamatay espirituwal dahil ang pera na ang naging sentro kaysa si Cristo.
At may mga mananampalataya na hindi na alam ang kaibahan ng tunay na biblical stewardship at spiritual manipulation.
Masakit itong pag-usapan.
Pero kailangan.
Dahil maraming simbahan ang nasira dahil sa pera.
Maraming pamilya ang nagkawatak-watak dahil sa pera.
Maraming lider ang bumagsak dahil sa kasakiman.
At maraming tao ang tuluyang lumayo kay Jesus dahil nasugatan sila ng maling paggamit ng pananalapi sa loob mismo ng simbahan.
Hindi iniiwasan ng Biblia ang usaping ito.
Sa katunayan, madalas magsalita si Jesus tungkol sa pera dahil ipinapakita nito kung sino talaga ang sinasamba ng puso.
Sa Mateo 6:21 sinabi ni Jesus:
“Sapagkat kung saan naroroon ang iyong kayamanan, doon din naman naroroon ang iyong puso.”
Ang salitang Griyego para sa “kayamanan” ay θησαυρός (thēsauros).
Ibig sabihin nito ay imbakan.
Taguan ng pinakamahalaga.
Hindi lang pera ang tinutukoy ni Jesus.
Pinapakita Niya kung ano talaga ang inuuna ng puso.
Dahil kung saan ka handang ibuhos ang lahat… iyon ang tunay mong sinasamba.
Kaya matindi ang atake ng kaaway pagdating sa pananalapi.
Hindi dahil masama ang pera.
Kundi dahil kayang palitan ng pag-ibig sa pera ang buong pagsuko sa Diyos.
Sinabi ni Apostol Pablo sa 1 Timoteo 6:10:
“Sapagkat ang pag-ibig sa salapi ay ugat ng lahat ng uri ng kasamaan.”
Ang salitang Griyego na φιλαργυρία (philargyria) ay nangangahulugang sobrang pagkagusto sa pilak o kayamanan.
Pansinin mo.
Hindi sinabi ni Pablo na masama ang pera.
Ang sinabi niya… ang sobrang pag-ibig dito ang nagbubukas ng pinto sa pagkawasak.
At totoo iyon.
May mga simbahan na naghiwalay dahil sa offerings.
May mga pagkakaibigan na namatay dahil sa pera.
May mga pastor na bumagsak dahil sa kasakiman.
At may mga mananampalatayang tuluyang nawalan ng gana sa pananampalataya dahil ang Gospel ay napalitan ng financial pressure.
Kaya bago tuluyang malito ang susunod na henerasyon tungkol sa tunay na biblical stewardship…
Kailangang malinaw itong sabihin.
At maaaring mas tumama ito sa puso mo kaysa inaasahan mo.
May ibang taong tahimik ding lumalaban sa parehong bagay.
Ang unang babala ay ang paggamit ng pagbibigay para manipulahin ang Diyos.
May mga taong tinuruan na kapag nagbigay sila nang malaki… obligado ang Diyos na pagyamanin sila.
Na parang ang offering ay investment para pilitin ang langit na magbigay ng material na kapalit.
Pero hindi iyon covenant.
Transactional religion iyon.
Sa Gawa 8, sinubukan ni Simon na bilhin ang kapangyarihan ng Diyos.
At matindi ang sagot ni Pedro:
“Mapahamak nawa kasama mo ang iyong salapi, sapagkat inakala mong mabibili mo ng salapi ang kaloob ng Diyos.”
Ang salitang Griyego para sa “mapahamak” ay ἀπώλεια (apōleia).
Pagkasira.
Pagkawasak.
Naiintindihan ni Pedro ang panganib.
Kapag iniisip ng tao na kayang kontrolin ng pera ang Diyos… nawawala ang tunay na pagsisisi.
Ang pagbibigay ay pagsamba.
Hindi panunuhol.
Hindi mo mabibili ang Banal na Espiritu.
Hindi mo mabibili ang anointing.
Hindi mo mapipilit ang Diyos gamit ang pera.
At oo… pinagpapala ng Diyos ang mapagbigay.
Pero ang biblical blessing ay mas malalim kaysa sasakyan, bahay, o social media success.
Minsan ang blessing ay kapayapaan sa gitna ng paghihirap.
Minsan ang blessing ay kalayaan mula sa kasakiman.
At minsan… ang pinakamalaking blessing ay ang hindi ibigay ng Diyos ang bagay na magiging diyos-diyosan mo.
Ang ikalawang babala ay ang pagpapabor sa mayaman habang hindi pinapansin ang mahirap.
Direktang kinondena ito ni Santiago.
Sa Santiago 2:2-4, pinagsabihan niya ang simbahan dahil mas mataas ang tingin nila sa mayaman.
Ang salitang Griyego na προσωπολημψία (prosōpolēmpsia) ay nangangahulugang favoritism.
Pagtingin sa halaga ng tao batay sa estado niya sa buhay.
At hanggang ngayon nangyayari pa rin ito.
Kapag mayamang donor… may espesyal na trato.
Kapag simpleng miyembro… halos walang nakakakita.
Kapag influential… may access.
Kapag mahirap… tahimik lang sa gilid.
Pero hindi sinusukat ng langit ang tao batay sa laman ng wallet.
Si Jesus mismo ay ipinanganak sa kababaang-loob.
Hindi sa palasyo.
Nagiging delikado ang simbahan kapag pera na ang basehan ng honor.
Dahil darating ang punto na mas poprotektahan na ang financial power kaysa katotohanan.
Ang ikatlong babala ay ang pamumuhay lampas sa kakayahan para lang magmukhang “blessed.”
Mas lumala ito sa panahon ng social media.
Maraming Kristiyano ang pagod na pagod na dahil pilit nilang pinapakita online na okay ang buhay nila.
Magandang damit.
Mamasa-masang posts.
Piliting image ng success.
Pero gabi-gabi kinakain ng anxiety.
Sabi sa Kawikaan 22:7:
“Ang nanghihiram ay alipin ng nagpapahiram.”
Ang salitang Hebreo para sa alipin ay עֶבֶד (‘eved).
Bondservant.
Nabubuhay sa ilalim ng kontrol.
Hindi lahat ng utang ay kasalanan.
Pero nagiging mapanganib ito kapag image na ang mas mahalaga kaysa wisdom.
May mga taong bumibili para magmukhang successful.
May iba namang gumagastos dahil sinusubukan nilang takpan ang emotional emptiness.
At may mga lider na lihim nang nalulunod sa pressure na panatilihin ang imahe ng “sobrang pinagpala.”
Pero walang kapayapaan sa pagpapanggap.
Hindi tayo tinawag ng Diyos para magmukhang mayaman.
Tinawag tayo para maging tapat.
Walang kahihiyan sa simpleng buhay.
Walang kahihiyan sa pagbangon ulit.
Walang kahihiyan sa pagsabing:
“Kailangan ko ng wisdom sa pananalapi.”
Ang ikaapat na babala ay ang paggamit sa generosity ng tao para sa personal na pakinabang.
Ito ang isa sa pinakamasakit na sugat sa modern Christianity.
Dahil sagrado ang spiritual authority.
Sa Ezekiel 34, kinondena ng Diyos ang mga shepherd na sarili lang nila ang pinapakain.
At nakakalungkot… paulit-ulit pa rin itong nangyayari.
May mga lider na gumagamit ng takot para makakuha ng pera.
May mga ministry na ginagamit ang emosyon ng tao para manipulahin sila.
May mga taong buong pusong nagbigay… tapos kalaunan nalaman nilang may corruption pala sa likod.
Totoong masakit iyon.
Pero ang abuse ay hindi ibig sabihin na mali na ang biblical generosity.
Ipinapakita lang nito kung bakit mahalaga ang accountability.
Ang tunay na shepherd… inuuna ang kaluluwa ng tao.
Hindi ang laman ng sobre.
Sinabi ni Pablo:
“Sapagkat hindi ang inyong ari-arian ang hinahanap ko kundi kayo.”
Ang tunay na lingkod ng Diyos… mas mahal ang tao kaysa offerings.
Palagi.
Ang ikalimang babala ay ang tuluyang pagsara ng puso sa generosity.
May mga tao na matapos masaktan sa church manipulation… ayaw nang magbigay kahit kailan.
Pero malinaw pa rin ang Biblia tungkol sa generosity.
Hindi dahil kailangan ng Diyos ang pera.
Kundi dahil binabago ng generosity ang puso.
Sa 2 Corinto 9:7:
“Iniibig ng Diyos ang nagbibigay na masaya.”
Ang salitang Griyego na ἱλαρός (hilaros) ay nangangahulugang joyful.
Maluwag sa loob.
Hindi pinipilit.
Hindi tinatakot.
Hindi ginuguilty.
Ang tunay na pagbibigay ay bunga ng pag-ibig.
At minsan… hindi pera ang pinakamalaking generosity.
Minsan oras.
Pagkain.
Panalangin.
Pagdamay.
Tahimik na pagtulong.
At sa mundong puro self-preservation… ang generosity ay nananatiling makapangyarihang pangangaral ng Ebanghelyo.
Ang ikaanim na babala ay ang pagtitiwala sa pera higit sa Diyos.
Puwedeng mangyari ito sa mayaman.
Puwedeng mangyari sa mahirap.
Puwedeng mangyari sa pastor.
Sa negosyante.
Sa kahit sino.
Dahil nagbibigay ang pera ng pakiramdam ng seguridad.
Pero puwedeng bumagsak ang ekonomiya.
Puwedeng mawala ang trabaho.
Puwedeng magkasakit.
Puwedeng magbago ang lahat sa isang iglap.
Sabi sa Awit 20:7:
“Ang iba ay nagtitiwala sa mga karo at ang iba naman ay sa mga kabayo, ngunit tayong lahat ay nagtitiwala sa pangalan ng Panginoon.”
Ngayon… iba na lang ang anyo ng “karo.”
Bank account.
Investments.
Status.
Connections.
Business.
Pero walang eternal doon.
Si Cristo lang.
At minsan hinahayaan ng Diyos ang uncomfortable seasons para ilantad kung saan talaga nakatayo ang tiwala natin.
Dahil maraming tao ang matatag lang ang faith habang stable ang finances.
Ang ikapitong babala ay ang pagkalimot sa eternity.
Ito marahil ang pinaka-mapanganib.
Dahil puwedeng ubusin ng tao ang buong buhay niya kakahabol ng temporary success.
Tinanong ni Jesus:
“Sapagkat ano ang mapapakinabang ng tao kung makamtan man niya ang buong sanlibutan ngunit mawala naman ang kanyang kaluluwa?”
Ang salitang Griyego na ψυχή (psychē) ay soul.
Inner life.
Tunay na pagkatao.
Posibleng yumaman ang tao habang unti-unting namamatay ang kaluluwa niya.
At maraming tao ang tahimik na nangyayari iyon.
May mayayamang hindi makatulog nang maayos.
May successful pero wasak emotionally.
May influential pero spiritually empty.
Dahil walang materyal na bagay ang kayang pumalit sa presensya ng Diyos.
Hindi pera.
Hindi applause.
Hindi influence.
Hindi fame.
Si Jesus lang ang kayang punuin ang kaluluwang pagod.
At baka iyon ang dahilan kung bakit nabasa mo ito ngayon.
Hindi para husgahan ka.
Kundi para gisingin ulit ang puso mo.
Para ipaalala na ang biblical stewardship ay hindi lang tungkol sa pera.
Tungkol ito sa pagsamba.
Katapatan.
Kababaang-loob.
Pagtitiwala.
At buong pagsuko kay Cristo.
Kung ikaw ay pagod na pagod na sa financial pressure… kung nasaktan ka ng church manipulation… kung nilalabanan mo ang greed, fear, pride, o anxiety… iniimbitahan ka pa rin ni Jesus na lumapit.
May grace pa rin.
May restoration pa rin.
May kapatawaran pa rin.
At hindi pa tapos ang kuwento mo.
Maging totoo ka.
May ibang taong nag-i-scroll ngayon na maaaring makahanap ng pag-asa dahil nakita nilang hindi sila nag-iisa.
Darating ang araw na mawawalan ng halaga ang lahat ng perang nahawakan mo… pero bawat kaluluwang nailapit mo kay Jesus Christ ay may eternal na epekto.
